subject: Dedicated inference reservation alignment for MLBridge - isolation & SLOs
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@mlbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated inference reservation alignment for MLBridge - isolation & SLOs

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps from both sides. I tried to capture the decisions we made and the open questions we agreed to answer.

High-level goals you shared
- Move inference for MLBridge’s clinical-triage model (seq len ~1024, median 256) to a dedicated pool to guarantee latency and isolation for HIPAA-sensitive traffic.
- Keep 99th-percentile token latency under 120ms for single-stream requests; target 95th < 50ms for bulk scoring.
- Reduce per-token cost vs current host by at least 25% while retaining current output quality.

Key pain points
- Noisy multi-tenant neighbors causing tail latency spikes during morning batch windows.
- Regulatory requirement to segregate PHI-processing models and retain audits for 12 months.
- Procurement needs a clear service description and an SLA they can attach to the Purchase Order.

What we think a good fit looks like (agreed during the call)
- Reserved dedicated GPU pool (4 x A100-equivalent slots initially) with tenant isolation and optional HSM/KMS for keys.
- Autoscaling headroom (burst) during scheduled batch windows and a canary rollout for the model change.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool; per-request latency SLO as above with credit-based remedies.

Open questions / action items (owners)
1) MLBridge to confirm average concurrent streams and peak batch concurrency (Alex) — helps with our sizing estimate.
2) Monica/Ben to produce a one-page procurement summary and a first-pass pricing ballpark (Monica / Ben) — attached: scoping-sheet.xlsx and an SLA draft (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf).
3) Jordan to provide sample contract language + timeline for Reserved Capacity PO (Jordan).
4) Safety/compliance checklist: MLBridge to share the list of data retention and audit export requirements (Alex / procurement).

Proposed next steps
- By Tue 2027-06-08: MLBridge sends concurrent/peak numbers and procurement contact.
- Wed 2027-06-09: Redwood will send a pricing ballpark and a mutual action plan (MAP) with canary schedule and milestones.
- Schedule technical walkthrough with Ben (SE) to discuss KV cache/quantization tradeoffs — propose Thu 2027-06-10 10:00am PT.

If that matches your view, I’ll lock the times and send calendar invites.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@mlbridge.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, procurement@mlbridge.ai
Date: 2027-06-06T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated inference reservation alignment for MLBridge - isolation & SLOs

Monica — thanks for the succinct recap, this is helpful. A few quick notes inline and below.

On sizing: we expect ~18 concurrent single-stream inference requests at peak and batch runs that spin up ~120 parallel scoring jobs (these are 4–6 minute jobs that run in a maintenance window). I’ll confirm with ops tomorrow but those are the numbers we use for capacity planning today.

On isolation: we do need hardware-level isolation for the PHI model (customer requirement) — software-multi-tenant isolation won’t pass our audit. HSM/KMS integration is a hard ask, same with 12mo audit exports.

On SLA and pricing: procurement wants a simple one-page SLA they can attach; the attached draft looks good as a starting point. For budgetary planning can you give a monthly range for a 4-slot reserved pool (ballpark, without discounts)? We’re doing internal modeling and need a number for the July planning cycle.

Requested additions
- Canary: we prefer a canary plan that runs 3% of traffic for 48 hours, with an automatic rollback on quality drift or latency regressions.
- Fallback: if reserved pool is unavailable, we need a routing policy that fails over to a pre-agreed multi-tenant fallback with lower SLA (and explicit cost delta).

I’m looped in on the Thu 6/10 slot; can Ben include an ops-oriented checklist (KV cache warmup, snapshotting) in that walkthrough?

Thanks — I’ll send procurement contact details in the morning.

—
Alex Chen
Senior ML Engineer, MLBridge
alex@mlbridge.ai

Alex — great, thanks for the numbers and the canary/fallback asks. Quick confirm and additions: 

1) Sizing: we’ll treat the baseline as 4 reserved slots and include an autoscaling burst policy to cover the 120-job batch window. Ben will enumerate how burst will affect tail latency and cost.

2) Isolation / compliance: we support physical isolation for the reserved pool and can integrate customer KMS (HSM path requires paperwork — Jordan will follow up with contract language and an estimated 2–3 week onboarding window).

3) Canary & rollback: agree with 3% for 48 hours — we’ll add automatic telemetry checks (latency, token-level quality signals) and define rollback triggers in the MAP.

4) Fallback routing: Redwood will provide a documented fallback route to the hosted multi-tenant endpoint with clear latency/cost delta. We’ll include an explicit cost per million tokens for both reserved and fallback paths in the pricing note.

Next steps and owners (updated)
- Alex: send procurement contact + confirmation of peak concurrency by Mon 2027-06-08 (Alex).
- Ben: ops/SE checklist and burst impact note for the Thu 6/10 call (Ben).
